status_summary: Executive Order 14159 (signed 2025-01-20), section 19, paused and ordered review of federal funding agreements with nongovernmental organizations that support removable aliens, and in February 2025 FEMA clawed back more than 80 million dollars from New York City under the Shelter and Services Program, which reimburses non-federal entities for sheltering noncitizens released from DHS custody; on 2025-04-01 FEMA terminated three Pima County awards under the program for no longer matching DHS priorities; a Manhattan judge declined on 2025-03-05 to order that money returned immediately. Bills to end the program and rescind its balances (S. 771 and H.R. 1668) were introduced on 2025-02-27; no enactment was found. On 2026-05-26 the Western District of Washington set aside the termination as applied to Washington and required FEMA to consider its reimbursement requests, without ordering payment. The redirect of the money to border and detention uses was not traced.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14159 (90 FR 8443) was signed; section 19 directs the Attorney General and the Secretary of Homeland Security to review and audit funding agreements with nongovernmental organizations that serve removable or illegal aliens, halt further payments pending review, end agreements found unlawful or wasteful, keep their funding out of the agencies' appropriations requests with OMB, and start recoupment where appropriate.

S. 771 and H.R. 1668, the End FEMA Benefits for Illegal Immigrants Act, were introduced to bar FEMA from running a program that funds sheltering by non-federal entities to relieve CBP holding facilities and to rescind unobligated transferred balances; S. 771 was referred to the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee and H.R. 1668 to several House committees the same day, with no later action.
A federal judge in Manhattan declined New York City's request for a temporary restraining order returning more than 80 million dollars in shelter funding that FEMA had clawed back in February 2025.

FEMA's Senior Official Performing the Duties of the Administrator issued a letter to Pima County, Arizona terminating three Shelter and Services Program grants (about 52.6 million dollars in total) with immediate effect for no longer matching DHS priorities, citing 2 CFR 200.340(a)(2), after a 2025-03-11 letter that barred new costs.
timeline.source: Pima County Board of Supervisors (copy of FEMA letter)

timeline.event: The State of Washington sued DHS and FEMA in the Western District of Washington (No. 2:25-cv-01401) over the end of its Shelter and Services Program award of about 4 million dollars.

Judge Rothstein granted Washington summary judgment in part on its Administrative Procedure Act claims (ECF 33) and entered judgment (ECF 34), holding the program termination policy contrary to law and arbitrary and capricious and setting it aside, with the termination of Washington's award, as applied to Washington; FEMA may not refuse to consider its reimbursement requests on the grounds held unlawful, and no payment was ordered.
